title: I Gave an AI Agent the Keys to My Life (Here's What Happened) — Radek Sienkiewicz (@velvetshark-com)
talk_summary: A personal-assistant agent (OpenClaw) maintainer describes growing his setup incrementally, one small workflow at a time, around a large markdown knowledge base (Obsidian, ~3000 notes) with search/memory, nightly maintenance jobs, and Discord channels per job type. The transferable core is operational discipline: deterministic scripts where no judgment is needed, explicit critical-rules files, nightly indexing/backup/update routines, and splitting brittle multi-step automations.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic scripts instead of LLM calls where no judgment is needed
takeaways.what_they_do: Routes routine plumbing to plain scripts ('if this happens, do this') and only invokes the LLM for judgment tasks like understanding context or making connections.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The scripts are just like, if this happens, do this. It's done. You don't even need judgment, so LLM is even skipped.

takeaways.technique: Critical-rules file pinned high in the agent config
takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps a separate CRITICAL_RULES.md referenced near the top of the agent file because rules buried in general memory/soul files were being forgotten.
Between ~3-6am the agent indexes everything, backs up, refreshes search/memory indexes, and pre-stages updates with verification scripts so the morning starts clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when I'm sleeping, again, my agent does everything so that it runs well. It indexes everything. It backs everything

takeaways.technique: One channel per recurring job type, promoted from general
takeaways.what_they_do: Starts everything in a general channel; when a conversation type recurs enough, it gets its own dedicated channel with its own context and rules.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if enough times I have a type a certain type of conversation, I added a specific channel for it

takeaways.what_they_do: Breaks 10-step automations into simpler ones or adds guardrails because long chains predictably break.

takeaways.technique: Markdown knowledge base with linked search/memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps ~3000 markdown notes and links them via multiple search layers (normal, QMD, workspace memory) so the agent can surface prior context and connections.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have search and memory. I have like normal search. I have QMD search for for Obsidian.
